title: Lay a curled drawing flat on the plan table and weight both ends
instruction: Lay the rolled site plan flat on the plan table, centred on the grey outline, using the two steel weights, then let go.
context: Construction site supervisors and architectural drafters (O*NET 47-1011.00, 17-3011.00) spread rolled drawings on a plan table and pin them open with weights. Cloth stays where it is laid, but a sheet stored rolled springs back: any end left free rolls back up. The skill is working out where the anchors go and in what order: each weight has to end on the sheet's last few centimetres, and the middle must stay pinned while the first half is opened.
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the station table top. (1) Plan table: fixed box 24 x 52 x 1.8 cm, white melamine, sRGB (0.96, 0.96, 0.94), friction 0.45 static / 0.40 dynamic, centred at (18, 0), top 1.8 cm above the table. Grey tape, sRGB (0.55, 0.55, 0.55), 5 mm wide and 0.3 mm thick, outlines an 18 x 40 cm rectangle centred at (18, 0) with its long side along y. (2) Site plan: a laminated drawing 18 cm along x by 40 cm along y, 1.5 mm thick, 48 g, white (0.96, 0.96, 0.94) with light-blue (0.80, 0.87, 0.98) linework, friction 0.35 / 0.30. It is modelled as 16 rigid 2.5 cm slats joined across the sheet by sprung hinges: rest bend 20 deg per hinge (a 7.2 cm natural curl radius), 0.05 N m/rad, damping 0.0008 N m s/rad, limits -30 to +60 deg. Start: centred on the outline at (18, 0), resting on its middle 15 cm with both ends rolled up and inward to about 8 cm above the plan table. (3) Two steel paperweights, weight_L and weight_R: bars 16 x 2.5 x 1.5 cm, 470 g each, dark grey steel (0.30, 0.30, 0.32) on a 2 mm green felt base (0.16, 0.32, 0.20), friction 0.25 / 0.22, lying on the plan table with the long side along x, centred at (18, +23.5) and (18, -23.5), just beyond the plan's ends.
scoring: Measured from link and bar poses every control step (20 Hz). A slat is flat when its centre is within 4 mm of its flat height and it is tilted less than 6 deg. An end is weighted when a weight's footprint covers at least 44 % of that end's last 2.5 cm slat (half the bar's width on it; the drawing's border margin) and the weight's underside is within 3 mm of the slat's top. Centred: the plan's centre within 15 mm of the outline centre and its long axis within 5 deg of y. A whole-run record (linkkit History in task.py), updated every control step and cleared only by the simulator reset, keeps the gate and the any-time rungs, so putting a weight back never erases a violation. Gate, checked first, gives 0: a weight's lowest point more than 5 mm below the station-table top at any time (a steel bar knocked off the bench); setting a weight down on the station table is allowed. Ladder, top down, scored at the end of the episode: 1.0 (success, must hold 1 s) the whole plan flat with both ends weighted, centred, no gripper pad within 30 mm of the plan or a weight, and every slat and both weights slower than 3 mm/s (from poses at 20 Hz) for the last 3 s, and both grippers 30 mm clear with tool points slower than 5 mm/s for the last 1 s (released); 0.75 the plan flat with both ends weighted at the end (hands anywhere); 0.5 at any time one end weighted with its whole half (8 slats) flat; 0.25 at any time one half (8 slats) flat out to its end slat; 0 otherwise. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: a top photo against the tape outline and a feeler gauge under each 2.5 cm line of the sheet.
reset_notes: Roll the plan back up for a few seconds and lay it on the plan table centred on the outline, ends up; it relaxes to its curl. Put both weights back on their marks at (18, +23.5) and (18, -23.5) cm with the long side along x. The plan table is fixed. object_jitter=0.
fidelity: The sheet is 16 rigid 25 mm slats with sprung hinges about one axis (a 72 mm curl, 0.05 N m/rad per hinge, about a 0.3 mm laminated sheet 18 cm wide), 48 g against about 27 g real, for solver stability. Corner curl and cockling are not modelled. The slats chatter at sub-millimetre amplitude in contact (a solver artefact), so stillness is measured from poses at 20 Hz; untouched, the curled sheet creeps about 0.3 mm/s. The weights are rigid felt-based steel bars.
